text:
sara: FYI seeing sustained 429s for several dedicated reserved pools in eu-west-1 starting ~10:12UTC. Customers on reserved pools getting throttled and we have queue growth.
infra-bot: ALERT: pool-saturation eu-west-1-A reserved-pool-42 > 92% admitted, 429 rate +18% in 5m. PodsPending: 12.
 tj: Which pools exactly? Is this cross-AZ or single-AZ pressure?
 sara: Mostly eu-west-1-A, some spill into -C. eu-west-1-B nodegroup shows scaledown failure earlier today (kops autoscale error). I can paste logs.
 maria: Pasting quick outputs:
 ```
$ kubectl get nodepool -n infra eu-west-1-b
NAME                     DESIRED  CURRENT  READY
eu-west-1-b               3        0        0

$ kubectl get pods -n redwood-dedicated | grep Pending | wc -l
12

Admission logs (snippet):
[2025-11-30T10:11:58Z] admission: reserved_pool=42 admit=false reason=capacity_threshold_reached
[2025-11-30T10:12:01Z] admission: reserved_pool=42 admit=false reason=az_imbalance_protection
```
 ops-oncall: Confirming, we're seeing retry spikes from the SDK too — clients are retrying aggressively which is amplifying queue.
 kevin: Looks like the allocator packed remaining instances into A after B nodegroup failed, which triggered per-AZ admission control threshold. We don't currently have cross-AZ spillover enabled for reserved pools.
 tj: Can we relax the per-AZ threshold temporarily or route -A traffic to other regions? What's fastest?
 sara: Short-term options: 1) bring eu-west-1-B nodepool back up (fastest), 2) temporarily bump reserved-pool admission limit for eu-west-1-A (risk: degraded latency for those pools), 3) route some requests to eu-west-2 but will cause increased latency for customers.
 infra-bot: ACTION: runbook 'reserved-pool-emergency-scale' invoked by ops-oncall at 10:18UTC.
 ops-oncall: Kicking option 1 now — scaling nodepool eu-west-1-b by +4. `gcloud container node-pools update eu-west-1-b --num-nodes=4`
 infra-bot: DEPLOYBOT: nodepool scale request accepted. New nodes registering...
 maria: After scale start: Pending dropped from 12 -> 4, 429s down to +4% but still above baseline. Observed a short tail latency increase for existing connections.
 tj: Need to prevent similar events — cause is twofold: (A) single nodepool failure reduced capacity in B; (B) admission control currently enforces strict AZ-local reserved quotas which prevents short-term spillover.
 kevin: Proposed mitigations: - implement temporary cross-AZ spill policy for reserved pools - add smoothing window for admission to avoid immediate hard 429 thresholds - make allocator prefer spreading reserved instances across AZs and failover nodes synchronous with autoscaler activities.
 sara: Customer impact: two enterprise tenants reported error bursts (IDs x-123, x-789). CS notified and we opened infra incident severity 2. Billing team flagged potential overage protection triggers.
 tj: Quick follow ups: 1) Ops to confirm nodepool fully healthy + report (ops-oncall), 2) Infra to add a short-term admission relaxation toggle (kevin/maria), 3) Prod metrics owner to tweak alerting to include AZ-imbalance score (sara).
 ops-oncall: Nodepool eu-west-1-b back to desired nodes, all nodes Ready as of 10:27UTC. 429s dropping to baseline by 10:30UTC.
 maria: I'll open a short RFC for cross-AZ spill policy and a runbook step to prefer immediate autoscaler restart on nodepool failures.
 kevin: I'll draft the admission smoothing change — small rate limiter with exponential backoff for rejected requests to avoid retry storms.
 sara: Thanks everyone — I'll file the incident ticket + postmortem. Marking this thread resolved for now. :thumbsup:
